native_result.query: In which century do Diversity in Pottery Decoration and Diversity in Pottery Form show opposite growth trends for the first time, with Pottery Decoration increasing significantly and Pottery Form declining simultaneously?
native_result.HypoA: In 1700 BCE, for the first time, Diversity in Pottery Decoration shows a significant increase while Diversity in Pottery Form experiences a notable decline. This marks a unique divergence in the growth trends of these two cultural capital variables.
native_result.HypoB: Diversity in Pottery Decoration and Diversity in Pottery Form first show opposite growth trends in the 18th century BCE (c. 1800-1700 BCE) [raw bin CE -1800 -> -1700; Delta measured into the CE -1700 anchor]. Decoration's Z value jumps from -0.48 to +0.97 (Delta +1.45; z +3.1 against the record's own 36 century-on-century changes, +4.4 excluding the 4100-4000 BCE series-edge transition) while Form drops from +0.74 to -1.13 (Delta -1.87; z -3.3 / -4.6). It is the only transition of 36 in the 4100-500 BCE record with Decoration up and Form down, under sign-only, |z|>=1/2/3 (edge included or excluded) and top-3/top-5 magnitude criteria, and the interpolated series confirms the onset inside 1800-1700 BCE (first qualifying 100-yr bin = CE -1800; rolling 200/300-yr slope onset CE -1758/-1752). Form's decline is a one-step drop that never recovers (pinned at -1.13 from 1700 to 500 BCE) and Decoration's rise is likewise a one-step increase that stays elevated (0.97, then 1.53 from 1000 BCE), so the divergence marks a structural break in a previously near-perfect coupling between the two diversity series (DeltaForm ~ 1.30 x DeltaDecoration, r = 0.9999 before; level correlation 1.00 -> 0.00 after; break residual = -532 pre-period residual sd). The transition coincides with the LN->OBA (Late Neolithic to Early Bronze Age) boundary in the period coding, noted as chronological context only, not as a cause.
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) Loaded data/time_series_data.csv (3601 x 36, CE -4100..-500) and QC'd the time axis: strictly monotonic, unique annual step = 1 yr, 0 duplicate CE, 0 gaps. 2) Established that PotteryDecoration/PotteryForm have only 37 non-missing values each, all on multiples of 100 CE (native 100-year/century anchors); verified *_inter is exact linear interpolation of those anchors (max abs error 2.2e-16) and used it ONLY for confirmation, never as 3601 independent points. 3) Cross-validated against data/capital.csv after comma-decimal parsing: CE = -BCE, Zkeverz = PotteryDecoration, ZKeform = PotteryForm, max abs diff 0.0 over 37 anchors; its 2 extra rows (BCE 4200/4300) are outside the window; capital.csv never pooled -> no double counting. Pollen file intentionally skipped (different variable and time coverage). 4) Computed century-on-century Deltas for the 36 transitions, z-scored twice (edge transition 4100->4000 BCE included vs excluded), ranked magnitudes, and scanned chronologically for the earliest transition with DeltaDecoration > 0 and DeltaForm < 0, recording all qualifiers to prove uniqueness and the absence of earlier ones. 5) Ran a 9-variant threshold sensitivity table (sign-only; |z|>=1/2/3 with edge in/out; top-3/top-5 magnitude). 6) Confirmation views: 100-yr bin means of the interpolated series and rolling OLS slopes (200/300 yr) at 0/0.25/0.5 sd thresholds, with per-episode slope magnitudes showing the zero-threshold early episodes (CE -3254/-3222/-3159/-3508) are interpolation noise at 0.1-0.5% of the transition's slope. 7) Extra statistics: 200k-permutation test of joint severity (p = 0.056) and structural-break coupling analysis. 8) Printed the full century-by-century series dump plus an ASCII overlay figure and exported century_change_table.csv, bin_mean_table.csv, rolling_slope_onset.csv and logs.
